subject: physics
title: Comparing Gravity and Electricity
welcome_lead: Two inverse-square laws side-by-side — similarities, differences and one big surprise.
meta_desc: A-Level Fields adventure on similarities and differences between gravity and electrostatics.
final_note: Gravity only attracts; electricity attracts or repels — that's why galaxies form differently from charges.

walkthroughs.body_html: F_grav = G m1 m2 / r² (attractive only). F_elec = Q1 Q2 / (4π ε₀ r²) (attract or repel). Both fall as 1/r², both with point-source field strength ∝ 1/r².
For two protons, electrostatic repulsion is about 10³⁶ times the gravitational attraction. Gravity dominates at large scales because mass is always positive.
Field strength g = GM/r² ↔ E = Q/(4π ε₀ r²). Potential V_grav = -GM/r ↔ V_elec = Q/(4π ε₀ r). Note sign convention.

If the distance between two masses doubles, what happens to the gravitational force between them?
options: Gravitational potential energy is negative because gravity does negative work.
It halves — gravitational force is inversely proportional to distance.
It doubles — more distance means more space for gravity to act through.
It quarters — gravitational force is inversely proportional to the square of the distance.

mcqs.q: Why is gravitational potential energy near a planet treated as negative?
options: Gravitational potential energy is negative because gravity does negative work.
Because the zero is defined at infinity; objects bound to the planet have lower (negative) potential energy than at infinity.
It doubles — more distance means more space for gravity to act through.
Gravitational potential energy is negative because gravity always points downwards.

mcqs.q: What does gravitational field strength at a point represent?
options: The force per unit mass that would act on a test mass placed at that point.
The mass of the object creating the field.
The total gravitational force at that point regardless of mass.
Gravitational potential energy is negative because gravity does negative work.
